the spoon theory is used among people with chronic illness and disability to explain how much energy/ability they have in a given day to do things. it's kind of an awkward shorthand (basically every day you're handed a random amount of spoons, and every time you do something, you trade in a spoon. some days you only have 3 spoons and can't get much done. some days you have 40. you have no control over how many spoons you get or when you run out on a given day).

like i said, it's awkward, but it's become really useful shorthand in explaining life with a chronic illness. i have rheumatoid arthritis and some days i'm 'out of spoons' by the time i get dressed in the morning and everything else is agony, and some days i'm able to work a full day and work out or go out with friends after, and i have no control over which day is which.
